findings.summary: The new rule fixes the task/foo-bar versus foo-bar case, but task lane IDs and hashed branch tokens can still occupy the same name.
evidence: In debug_followup_routing.py, a lowercase-slug task lane ID is returned unchanged; another branch maps to its slug plus the first 8 hex characters of its raw-branch SHA-256.
For a non-task branch B with slug S and hash h, B maps to S-h. A distinct branch task/S-h also maps to S-h because S-h is itself a lowercase slug.
When both branches need a follow-up record for the same title and date, the shared token can produce the same record name.

The collision test covers task/foo-bar versus foo-bar but not a task lane ID equal to another branch's slug-plus-hash. Its docstring claims names never collide across distinct branches, which the examples do not establish.
findings.action: Make task-lane and other-branch tokens disjoint, or otherwise ensure the task-lane exception cannot match a hashed branch token. Add a test using task/<slug>-<hash-of-raw-branch> and align the test claim and release notes with the resulting guarantee.
